    == sha("work/compact-caller/specialist-plar-read.json"),
    "receipt_names_same_snapshot": receipt["path"] == compact["path"] and receipt["sha256"] == compact["sha256"],
    "receipt_identities": receipt["asset_id"] == "queue.working" and receipt["requirements_hash"] == R

evidence.declaration_text:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
```

requirements.name: geometry
requirements.check: Decode assets/working.png as exactly 64x16: four horizontal 16x16 cells at x=0,16,32,48 with no gutters or added canvas between or around the cells (transparent margin inside a cell is composition, not padding). Consumer basis (unchanged original module src/queue-view.ts lines 4 and 9; identical constants in the proposed successor module lines 8 and 13): running frames 4 (the sheet's cell count, unchanged under either preference), display.cell [16,16] and frameMs 100. Fixture behaviour, descriptive only and scoped to this successor destination as designed: the successor fixture draws only when width == 16*frames and height == 16, slices frame*16,0,16,16 and derives the frame from frameAt() (floor(elapsed/100) mod 4 when animating; the held cell otherwise).
requirements.reason: Fresh decode records exact target geometry: Working64x16, Retry/Paused16x16. All actual rendered crops match source dimensions and horizontal cell rectangles.

requirements.name: transparent-exterior-measured
requirements.check: MEASURED record (mechanical/local, diagnostic): retain every cell's alpha histogram and exact RGBA component boxes (zero-based, half-open). FLAG for visual review any alpha>0 component touching all four cell edges, or any single alpha>0 component covering more than half of the cell's 256 pixels. The flag is a diagnostic proxy for a canvas matte or grey tile and is NOT a rejection condition (a corner-to-corner X or full-span glyph legitimately touches all four edges with a transparent exterior). RGB values of alpha-0 pixels are not significant. PROPOSAL (seed-rotation construction only): mechanical REJECTION is decidable only under that construction, where each cell's alpha channel must equal that of cw^k(seed) under dst(x,y)=src(y,15-x) (for the current seed 21f5baca...: measured 224 alpha-0 / 32 alpha-255 pixels per cell). Outside that construction the measured record carries no rejection rule.
requirements.reason: Fresh per-cell alpha histograms, exact RGBA boxes and4-connected components retained. Flags are diagnostic only. Working seed-rotation alpha and visibleRGBA equality pass all4cells under the scoped seed-rotation proposal; selective/full alpha remains permitted.

requirements.name: transparent-exterior-visual
requirements.check: VISUAL record (visual/visual; the deciding rule): viewed at 1x and 3x on #172336, the exterior of every frame, including the held cell when stationary shows the panel with no unintended matte, tile, plate, halo or fringe; a deliberate opaque backing shape is acceptable only when it is part of the mark's recorded design and the exterior stays transparent. Partial alpha on mark pixels is permitted; binary alpha is not required. The rejected generated frame whose background held 193 opaque #808080 pixels is the failure class, not the definition of the rule.
requirements.reason: Viewed native and3x colour/gray marks and rendered panel exterior. Negative space remains panel; no unintended solid tile, fringe or halo. Alpha diagnostics were not used as the deciding visual rule.

evidence.declaration_text:
Run one pixel-art command on a drawing or image you already made. This is
the engine's own command line: it checks work, explains it and improves it.

Commands: check and explain (read-only):
- lint <id> [--rules outline_gap,orphan_pixel,…] — pixel-art defects, each
  naming the node and command that drew them
- inspect <id> --region x0,y0,x1,y1 --scale 10 — a zoomed crop with its
  exact colours
- measure <id> --at x,y — what is at a pixel and who drew it
- explain <id> — resolved geometry, per-command footprints, before rendering
- motion / storyboard / silhouette / reveal / clusters / parts <id> — reports
- score <id> — a 0-100 pixel-art discipline score with a breakdown
- compare <id> <id> — two results side by side
Improve (returns a NEW drawing id):
- shade <id> --band 2 --light=-1,-1 — banded shading along a colour ramp
- selout <id> — selective outlining; reoutline / clean-lines / aa / mirror
- cluster <id> --at x,y --action recolor --color <name> — one guarded cluster
- repair <id> — deterministic cleanup of drift, strays, fringe and noise
Sheets and frames (returns a NEW image id):
- split <image> --grid 3x3 — a sprite sheet, strip or grid as an animation,
  one frame per cell (columns x rows)
- join <image> <image> … [--as sheet|rows|animation] [--columns n] — pictures
  or animations as one sprite sheet, one per row, or one animation
- scale <image> --by 4 — the same picture or animation bigger, each pixel a
  4x4 block (a sticker, a print); nothing is redrawn
A result comes back as an image in the reply AND as a no-auth URL the reply
prints, `/mcp/pixel-tools/<id>/image.png` (`frames.png` for the frames of a
multi-frame one) — so a sheet you joined is both readable inline and
downloadable. Sheets hold at most 1024 px a side; `join` refuses a larger
one rather than shrinking the art, and says how many frames do fit.
Craft operations need colour ramps: run `extract-palette <id>` first, then
pass `--ramps skin=dark,mid,light`.
Authoring: `edit <id> --changes '[…]'` applies exact pixel operations and
`draw <id> --recipe '{…}'` builds or revises a layered scene; both take JSON
whose fields are NOT listed here. Colours in that JSON are always `#RRGGBB`
or `#RRGGBBAA` with alpha `00` or `ff` — `rgb()` and bare hex are refused,
and nothing strips the `#`, since argv is a JSON list rather than a shell
line. Every `edit` change carries `operation`, `layer`, `frames` (ONE-based)
and `reason`; coordinates are zero-based and a `region` is `[x0,y0,x1,y1]`
inclusive. Then its own fields: `patch_pixels` takes `pixels`, a list of
`[x,y,expected,replacement]` (1-10000, each assigned only where the pixel
already holds `expected`, so a mismatch fails the pass); `copy_region` takes
`source_layer`, `source_frame`, `region`, `at` `[x,y]`; `map_colors` takes
`region` and `colors` `{"#from":"#to"}` (alpha must match); `flood_fill`
`seed`/`expected`/`color`; `brush` `points` plus `color`; `outline` `mode`
(outside|inside|recolor|erase). The full contracts and any command's flags
are one free call away: `describe edits | paint | outline | draw | animation
| motion | scenes | review`, `<command> -h`, `describe cli`.
Free for subscribers.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__pixelart_workbench(args: {
  // One command line, e.g. 'lint <drawing_id> --rules outline_gap' or ['edit', '<id>', '--changes', '[…]']. Omit it for the playbook. A subject is an id or an image reference — never a file path; the server writes the output and returns a new id. A reference is `character:<id>:<direction>` for a rotation, `character:<id>:<direction>:<animation>` for every frame of that animation (the display name, type or [group: ...] id get_character prints), the same two forms for `object:<id>` (a one-direction object's direction is the literal `unknown`), `gallery:<id>`, `job:<id>`, `upload:<id>`, a data URL, an https link or base64. That is how a stored animation's pixels come back inline without downloading anything. Start with 'describe cli' for the full command list.
  argv?: string | Array<string> | null;
  // low (default): act directly, fewest tokens — one decisive image per result. high: think openly — fuller evidence and a review checklist; write your plan and observations in `notes`. Use the mode the user asked for.
  mode?: "low" | "high";
  // What you observed and what this step should achieve, in a few sentences (high mode: always; low: optional). On the first call, include the user's request. Stored with the step to improve these tools.
  notes?: string | null;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```
evidence.schema_representation: JSON Schema projection of the exposed TypeScript argument declaration: argv string | string[] | null, mode 'low' | 'high', notes string | null; additionalProperties false
evidence.subject_transport: Each argv subject is a data:image/png;base64 URL of the exact retained seed bytes (declaration: a subject is an id or an image reference, including a data URL, an https link or base64; never a file path). Base64 computed from the artifact file and verified to round-trip to the same sha256.

content.text: Saving the refresh return, then capturing byte-exact pixl_source returns for both locators via the frozen kit's local MCP server, and inspecting the child's receipt and specialist result.

input.command:
cd "/c/Users/ryanf/AppData/Local/Temp/pixl readiness claude clean jnw4uxrb/consumer" && F="/c/Users/ryanf/.claude/projects/C--Users-ryanf-AppData-Local-Temp-pixl-readiness-claude-clean-jnw4uxrb-consumer/0510b038-b18b-4fbc-aafe-c19b95d7dba6/tool-results/mcp-pixl-local-pixl_plar_read-1794609789998.txt" && test ! -e work/compact-caller/refresh.json && cp "$F" work/compact-caller/refresh.json && test ! -e work/compact-caller/helper_source_reads.py && cat > work/compact-caller/helper_source_reads.py <<'EOF'
"""Parent caller helper: retrieve details_ref and resume_ref byte-exactly through the frozen kit's
local MCP server (stdio JSON-RPC, same route as missing_capability_probe.py). Read-only.
Writes only fresh files under work/compact-caller. Locators are taken from compact.json, not retyped."""
import hashlib, json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
out = root / "work/compact-caller"
compact = json.loads((out / "compact.json").read_text("utf-8"))
reqs = []
for i, (name, ref, budget) in enumerate((("details", compact["details_ref"], 65536), ("resume", compact["resume_ref"], 8192)), start=1):
    reqs.append({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "pixl_source", "arguments": {
        "path": ref["path"], "expect": ref["sha256"], "start": ref["start"], "end": ref["end"], "budget": budget, "scope": "project"}}})
proto = out / "source-reads-protocol.jsonl"
if proto.exists(): raise SystemExit("protocol output exists; use a fresh name")
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(root / "installed pixl/scripts/pixl.py"), "mcp", "--root", str(root)],
                   input="".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in reqs).encode("utf-8"), capture_output=True)
with proto.open("xb") as s: s.write(p.stdout)
with proto.with_suffix(".stderr.txt").open("xb") as s: s.write(p.stderr)
responses = {r["id"]: r for r in (json.loads(l) for l in p.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip())}
lines = (root / compact["details_ref"]["path"]).read_text("utf-8").split("\n")
summary = {"returncode": p.returncode, "reads": {}}
for i, name in ((1, "details"), (2, "resume")):
    res = responses[i]["result"]
    text = res["content"][0]["text"]
    target = out / f"{name}-read.json"
    if target.exists(): raise SystemExit(f"{target} exists")
    target.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
    obj = json.loads(text)
    ref = compact[f"{name}_ref"]
    physical = "\n".join(lines[ref["start"] - 1: ref["end"]]) + "\n"
    summary["reads"][name] = {
        "saved": f"work/compact-caller/{name}-read.json",
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
        "isError": res.get("isError", False),
        "returned": {k: obj[k] for k in ("sha256", "start", "end", "bytes")},
        "locator": ref,
        "text_utf8_bytes": len(obj["text"].encode("utf-8")),
        "bytes_match_locator": len(obj["text"].encode("utf-8")) == ref["bytes"],
        "text_equals_physical_lines": obj["text"] == physical,
        "trailing_member_comma_preserved": obj["text"].rstrip("\n").endswith(","),

"""Parent caller helper: retrieve details_ref and resume_ref byte-exactly through the frozen kit's
local MCP server (stdio JSON-RPC, same route as missing_capability_probe.py). Read-only.
Writes only fresh files under work/compact-caller. Locators are taken from compact.json, not retyped."""
import hashlib, json, pathlib, subprocess, sys
root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
out = root / "work/compact-caller"
compact = json.loads((out / "compact.json").read_text("utf-8"))
reqs = []
for i, (name, ref, budget) in enumerate((("details", compact["details_ref"], 65536), ("resume", compact["resume_ref"], 8192)), start=1):
    reqs.append({"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": i, "method": "tools/call", "params": {"name": "pixl_source", "arguments": {
        "path": ref["path"], "expect": ref["sha256"], "start": ref["start"], "end": ref["end"], "budget": budget, "scope": "project"}}})

p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", str(root / "installed pixl/scripts/pixl.py"), "mcp", "--root", str(root)],
                   input="".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in reqs).encode("utf-8"), capture_output=True)
with proto.open("xb") as s: s.write(p.stdout)
with proto.with_suffix(".stderr.txt").open("xb") as s: s.write(p.stderr)
responses = {r["id"]: r for r in (json.loads(l) for l in p.stdout.splitlines() if l.strip())}
lines = (root / compact["details_ref"]["path"]).read_text("utf-8").split("\n")
summary = {"returncode": p.returncode, "reads": {}}
for i, name in ((1, "details"), (2, "resume")):
    res = responses[i]["result"]
    text = res["content"][0]["text"]
    target = out / f"{name}-read.json"
    if target.exists(): raise SystemExit(f"{target} exists")
    target.write_bytes(text.encode("utf-8"))
    obj = json.loads(text)
    ref = compact[f"{name}_ref"]
    physical = "\n".join(lines[ref["start"] - 1: ref["end"]]) + "\n"
    summary["reads"][name] = {
        "saved": f"work/compact-caller/{name}-read.json",
        "sha256": hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest(),
        "isError": res.get("isError", False),
        "returned": {k: obj[k] for k in ("sha256", "start", "end", "bytes")},
        "locator": ref,
        "text_utf8_bytes": len(obj["text"].encode("utf-8")),
        "bytes_match_locator": len(obj["text"].encode("utf-8")) == ref["bytes"],
        "text_equals_physical_lines": obj["text"] == physical,
        "trailing_member_comma_preserved": obj["text"].rstrip("\n").endswith(","),
        "json_pointer": ref["json_pointer"],
    }

w = root / "work/compact-caller"


def sha(p):
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


report = {"checks": [], "failures": []}


def check(ok, msg):
    report["checks"].append({"ok": bool(ok), "check": msg})
    if not ok:
        report["failures"].append(msg)


REF_KEYS = {"path", "sha256", "role", "start", "end", "bytes", "json_pointer"}


def walk(obj, where, acc):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        if {"path", "sha256"} <= set(obj) <= REF_KEYS and isinstance(obj.get("sha256"), str) and len(obj["sha256"]) == 64:
            acc.append((where, obj["path"], obj["sha256"]))
        for k, v in obj.items():
            walk(v, where + "/" + str(k), acc)
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for i, v in enumerate(obj):
            walk(v, where + "/" + str(i), acc)


def verify_refs(rel):
    doc = json.loads((root / rel).read_text("utf-8"))
    acc = []
    walk(doc, rel, acc)
    for where, p, h in acc:
        f = root / p
        check(f.is_file() and sha(f) == h, where + ": " + p + " sha256 matches")
    return doc, len(acc)


cr, n = verify_refs("work/compact-caller/CALLER-RESULT.json")
check(n >= 15, "CALLER-RESULT references verified: %d" % n)
check(len((w / "CALLER-RESULT.json").read_bytes()) <= 8192, "CALLER-RESULT.json <= 8192 UTF-8 bytes")
for k in ["native_child", "compact", "receipt", "parent_receipt", "details_read", "resume_read", "refresh", "specialist_result",
          "errors", "unknown_recovery", "stale_recovery", "same_snapshot", "assignment_status", "production_next",
          "unknown_job_id", "unknown_job_state", "scope", "unresolved", "next_action"]:
    check(k in cr, "CALLER-RESULT has field " + k)
check(set(cr["errors"]) == {"invalid_authoring", "stale_local_state", "unavailable_observation", "uncertain_remote_result", "missing_capability"},
      "five error categories present")
sr, n = verify_refs("work/compact-caller/SPECIALIST-RESULT.json")
check(n >= 6, "SPECIALIST-RESULT references verified: %d" % n)
check(sr["status"] == "partial" and sr["native_child"]["agent_id"] == "ab352c80d7f534aae", "specialist result partial, actual child id")

compact = json.loads((w / "compact.json").read_text("utf-8"))
receipt = json.loads((w / "receipt.json").read_text("utf-8"))
parent = json.loads((w / "parent-receipt.json").read_text("utf-8"))
snap = root / compact["path"]
check(compact["sha256"] == receipt["sha256"] == parent["sha256"] == sha(snap), "compact, receipt and parent receipt name the same snapshot bytes")
for k in ("asset_id", "requirements_hash", "state_hash", "next", "scope", "path"):
    check(compact[k] == receipt[k] == parent[k], "receipt field identical: " + k)
hand = json.loads(snap.read_text("utf-8"))
details = json.loads((w / "details.json").read_text("utf-8"))
check(hand["details"] == details, "handoff /details equals details.json")
lines = snap.read_text("utf-8").split("\n")
for name in ("details", "resume"):
    r = json.loads((w / (name + "-read.json")).read_text("utf-8"))
    ref = compact[name + "_ref"]
    phys = "\n".join(lines[ref["start"] - 1:ref["end"]]) + "\n"
    check(r["text"] == phys and len(r["text"].encode("utf-8")) == ref["bytes"] == r["bytes"] and r["sha256"] == ref["sha256"],
          name + "-read exact slice, bytes and hash match locator")
    check(r["text"].rstrip("\n").endswith(","), name + "-read trailing member comma preserved")
    member = json.loads("{" + r["text"].rstrip("\n").rstrip(",") + "}")
    check(member[name] == hand[name], name + "-read parses to handoff " + ref["json_pointer"])

refresh = json.loads((w / "refresh.json").read_text("utf-8"))
cont = refresh["production"]["continuation"]
check(cont["state_hash"] == compact["state_hash"] and refresh["requirements_hash"] == compact["requirements_hash"]
      and cont["store"] == compact["store"] and cont["action"] == compact["next"], "refresh identities equal compact identities")
check(refresh["production"]["pending_jobs"] == [] and refresh["production"]["revision"] == 108, "refresh: no pending jobs, revision 108")
stale = json.loads((w / "stale-recovery.json").read_text("utf-8"))
check(stale["production"]["continuation"]["state_hash"] == compact["state_hash"], "stale-recovery read matches compact state hash")

proto = [json.loads(l) for l in (w / "missing-capability-protocol.jsonl").read_text("utf-8").splitlines() if l.strip()]
check(proto[1]["result"]["isError"] is True and proto[1]["result"]["structuredContent"]["error"] == "unknown_tool",
      "missing-capability raw protocol retains isError unknown_tool")
check("pixl_missing_capability_probe" not in {t["name"] for t in proto[0]["result"]["tools"]}, "tools/list lacks the probed tool")
ur = json.loads((w / "unknown-recovery.json").read_text("utf-8"))
pre = json.loads((w / "unknown-jobs-precheck.json").read_text("utf-8"))
check(ur["result"] == pre and ur["result"]["jobs"][0]["state"] == "unknown"
      and ur["result"]["hash"] == "3ab0c1633edbf21977744bab59eb2a15b2cd8dc81424ea3cfe6c569d5f35e0a9" and len(ur["result"]["jobs"][0]["events"]) == 1,
      "unknown job unchanged before/after rejected duplicate dispatch")
check(not (w / "intentionally-missing.txt").exists(), "intentionally-missing.txt not created")

preserved = {"compact.json": "ff5c2289915ce12c26cc69073759f6254e154d341a631465d262ff8720900687",
             "details.json": "92682b133f09898b20e620fd0e9aea94f2aad3b5aae511f2ceec9defa87a3dc2",

             "specialist-plar-read.json": "3dccfd43851c41b036281bf4def05789a50791c91c28dd2b19c778d4b2ff34f2"}
for f, h in preserved.items():
    check(sha(w / f) == h, "session-1 file preserved: " + f)
prior = {"work/artistic-revision/SPECIALIST-RESULT.json": "e65ee7d76927a5ea1226d56565f860fae35fb24767d5a3e6c2034a13a4222a4c",
         "work/artistic-revision/CALLER-RESULT.json": "f5f13234e9c735256a890bd5023fa8b95a641181d6feb77b1381600d89e46821",
         "assets/working.png": "cf101610108f5a708987dfeb1a86ae9921525464d24c19953a889e20603176dc",
         ".pixl/handoffs/e560a32dcaf31134abbb81b661a0a2fc12824461a049c90b1c780cc01464273d.json": "e560a32dcaf31134abbb81b661a0a2fc12824461a049c90b1c780cc01464273d"}
for f, h in prior.items():

check(len(list((root / ".pixl/handoffs").iterdir())) == 11, "handoff directory still 11 files (no new snapshot this session)")
